    Run major home appliances with 7200W of rated power (14,400W surge). Supports both 120V and 240V for power more devices, even a 5-ton AC for comfortable indoor temperatures or a water heater for a hot shower.

    Compatible with both high-and low-voltage solar panels, recharge in about 2 hours with up to 4000W input, staying powered in home or RV.

    11 Years of Reliable Power

    FAQ

    About 5000 Plus
    About Solar Panel
    About Battery Pack 5000 Plus
    About Smart Transfer Switch
    About Installation

    • Can the E5000 Plus be used in parallel with the E2000 Plus, E1000 Plus, or their additional power packs simultaneously?

      No, they are distinct products with varying voltage, current, and power specifications, rendering them incompatible for simultaneous parallel use.

    • Does the E5000 Plus support compatibility and connection with the E2000 Plus and similar models?

      The E5000 Plus and E2000 Plus can charge each other by connecting each unit's AC input to the other’s AC output.

    • Can the E5000 Plus be used in parallel with other Jackery products that support parallel usage? Can products from other brands be used in parallel with Jackery products?

      The E5000 Plus supports parallel usage of two E5000Plus units via STS. It does not support parallel usage with other Jackery power station products or with products from other brands.

    • How would I integrate the E5000 Plus into my existing system? Can the E5000 Plus be connected to our home circuit system and work as UPS?

      Yes, E5000 Plus supports connecting to your home circuit system and you can insert it into by TS/Inlet box/STS.If the E5000 Plus is solely connected to home circuits and the Online UPS mode is selected in the APP, it will immediately power on upon detecting a power outage. If the E5000 Plus is connected to the Jackery Smart Transfer Switch, the response time in the event of a power failure will be 20 milliseconds due to the Transfer Switch's capabilities.

    • Is the E5000 Plus expandable? How to increase the capacity of the E5000 Plus？

      The Jackery E5000 Plus is expandable, offering an initial 5kWh. Connecting one 5000 Plus unit with a E5000 Plus Battery Pack provides 10kWh, expandable up to 5 Battery Packs for a total of 30kWh. With two E5000 Plus units and 10 Battery Packs, you can reach a maximum of 60kWh. Please look up the maximum capacity allowed in your jurisdiction prior to ordering.

    • Is the exterior material fireproof? What is the fire-proof level?

      It uses the highest 94V-0 fireproof material required by American UL

    • Why can't the 5000 Plus charge via AC input?

      When connected to the STS, the 120V AC input cannot be used to charge the E5000 Plus.

    • How long can the 5000 Plus power common household appliances?

      The runtime of the Jackery 5000 Plus depends on the power consumption of the appliances being used.

      For example, a 170L household refrigerator (15–520W) can run for approximately 8 hours in freezing mode and up to 110 hours in insulation mode. A compact refrigerator (90W) can operate for about 26 hours.

      A central air conditioner (2200–3050W) can run for around 2 hours in cooling mode and 1.7 hours in heating mode, while a wall-mounted AC unit (900W) can run for about 4.5 hours.

      These figures are based on Jackery lab tests and may vary depending on the actual power draw of the appliances and environmental conditions. The data is for reference only.

    • Can the Explorer 5000 Plus be connected to third-party solar panels, generators, or fuel-powered devices?

      Yes, the Explorer 5000 Plus can be connected to third-party solar panels or fuel-powered generators, provided they meet the required input interface and connection standards. For safe and efficient operation, please ensure the voltage, current, and connector type are compatible with the Explorer 5000 Plus. Detailed input specifications can be found in the product’s technical parameters.

      While third-party access is possible, Jackery recommends using official accessories to ensure optimal performance and maintain warranty coverage.

    • Can I use this power station with medical devices, life-support equipment, business-critical systems, or other essential equipment?

      For safety reasons, Jackery portable power stations are not recommended for use with medical devices, life-support equipment, data servers, or other applications where a power interruption could result in personal injury, loss of life, or significant property damage.

      We do not recommend using this product to power equipment such as:

      Medical devices or any equipment related to life support or personal safety.

      Critical public infrastructure or public service equipment.

      Business-critical equipment, including data servers and other systems that require uninterrupted power.

      Any other equipment where a power interruption could lead to serious safety risks or significant property damage.

      Although Jackery products are designed to provide reliable power, interruptions may occur due to battery depletion, overload protection, environmental conditions, or other unexpected factors. For this reason, we do not recommend using the product for life-critical, safety-critical, or mission-critical applications.

      In addition, individuals with an implanted cardiac pacemaker or other implanted medical devices are advised not to use this product, as stated in our safety instructions.

      For your safety, we do not recommend using Jackery products for any of the applications listed above.

    • Is E5000 Plus compatible with all the Jackery Solar Panels?

      The charging port of the E5000 Plus has dimensions of 8020, making it compatible with all the solar panels we currently have on sale. If you have older versions of solar panels with capacities of 60W/100W/200W, you will need to use a 7909-to-8082 adapter.

    • Can the Explorer 5000 Plus be used with outdoor solar panels while the main unit stays indoors? Are extended cables available, and is there a recommended length limit?

      Yes, you can extend the connection indefinitely by purchasing the Jackery 5M DC extension cable, though longer connections may reduce solar charging efficiency.

    • Can the E5000 Plus Battery Pack charge my device separately?

      No, the Battery Pack need to be connected to the E5000 Plus power station for charging.

    • Can I use this power station with medical devices, life-support equipment, business-critical systems, or other essential equipment?

      For safety reasons, Jackery portable power stations are not recommended for use with medical devices, life-support equipment, data servers, or other applications where a power interruption could result in personal injury, loss of life, or significant property damage.

      We do not recommend using this product to power equipment such as:

      Medical devices or any equipment related to life support or personal safety.

      Critical public infrastructure or public service equipment.

      Business-critical equipment, including data servers and other systems that require uninterrupted power.

      Any other equipment where a power interruption could lead to serious safety risks or significant property damage.

      Although Jackery products are designed to provide reliable power, interruptions may occur due to battery depletion, overload protection, environmental conditions, or other unexpected factors. For this reason, we do not recommend using the product for life-critical, safety-critical, or mission-critical applications.

      In addition, individuals with an implanted cardiac pacemaker or other implanted medical devices are advised not to use this product, as stated in our safety instructions.

      For your safety, we do not recommend using Jackery products for any of the applications listed above.

    • How much does it cost for installation of the Smart Transfer Switch?

      The cost is typically 1500-2000 USD, but it may vary depending on your location and specific home conditions. For details, you can discuss with our certified installer after placing an order or consult a local electrician.

    • Does the Smart Transfer Switch accomodate more than one E5000 Plus?

      Yes, the Jackery Smart Transfer Switch supports connecting two Explorer 5000 Plus units in parallel, allowing for increased power capacity and redundancy in your home power system.

    • Why doesn't the E5000 Plus start charging immediately after connecting to the Smart Transfer Switch?

      By default, the Smart Transfer Switch automatically charges the E5000 Plus only when its battery level drops below a preset value. To charge immediately, please use the app: App > Smart Transfer Switch > Power Station > Charge now. To change the default preset value, use the app: App > Smart Transfer Switch > Working Modes > Set Backup Reserve.

    • Why do some circuits not have power after the mains power is restored?

      After the mains power is restored, the circuits that were disconnected based on backup power priority during the outage will not be automatically turned on to reduce the risk of electric shock. Customers need to manually turn on the disconnected circuits.

    • Can I use my own electrician or by myself?

      Yes, you may use your own certified electrician, or handle the STS installation yourself (if you are certified), at your own expense. We highly recommend contacting Jackery for training and certification before proceeding with the installation. You can also refer to the STS User Guide, FAQs, and installation videos available on our website.

    • I’ve completed the STS Installation Request Form and contacted the installation company but haven’t received a response. What should I do?

      Ensure that the email and phone number you provided are correct. Also, check your Spam folder. If you still don’t receive a response, contact the installation company or Jackery again. A representative will reach out to you.

    • What information do I need for my installation?

      Jackery or a third-party company will send you a STS Installation Request Form to begin the installation process. You should prepare your order information, contact information including your email, phone number and address for the installation.

    • Who should I contact for my installation—Jackery or a third-party company?

      If you choose to use Jackery’s resource for your installation, please fill out the online STS Installation Request Form or contact our Customer Service at hello@jackery.com or 888.502.2236. STS Installation Request Form link: https://docs.google.com/forms/d/1ZIFnrwCOq6X9QsRPvP_VyLhHgLE5IyzM4wMMFVOgBD8/viewform?edit_requested=true

    • What should the electrician do if the on-site conditions differ from expectations?

      The electrician should immediately contact both the customer and the installation company to discuss solutions and adjust the installation plan accordingly.

    • What should I do if I have concerns or I'm dissatisfied with the quote?

      The customer can discuss the details of the quote with the electrician or the installation company to seek reasonable adjustments.

    • What if the electrician is unable to provide service on time or cannot be contacted?

      The customer should contact Jackery or the installation company, who will assist in reaching the electrician or assign a new one.

    • The installation company scheduled an electrician for me, but I haven’t heard from them. What should I do?

      Check your Spam folder first. If there’s still no response, contact the installation company or Jackery again for assistance.

    • Does Jackery provide installation services for the STS?

      Jackery does not install the STS but we’ve partnered with third-party companies to provide installation services for U.S. customers in over 40 states.

    • Where Can I Find More Information About Installing the Jackery Smart Transfer Switch (STS)?

      If you need detailed guidance on installing the Jackery Smart Transfer Switch (STS), please visit installation service page at: https://www.jackery.com/pages/smart-transfer-switch-installation-service. This page provides service options, and additional support to ensure a smooth setup process.

Many noted fast charging and expandability with additional batteries. Positive feedback highlighted ease of use and quality construction. Some concerns included software quirks, solar panel compatibility issues with input terminals, heavy weight (123 lbs), and short solar panel cables.

    Purchased the 5000 so the wife could plug it into

    Purchased the 5000 so the wife could plug it into the manual transfer switch and just turn it on. We've had 5 power outages this year so far. I was so impressed I purchased an expansion battery. Power goes out, plug it in to the transfer switch, turn it on and flip ithe transfer switches to Generator. It's running a tv/DVD player, two inverter window ACs, a freezer and fridge, LED lights, two Coway airmegas, two small fans, some office equipment, two CPAP machines, a nebulizer, two pond pumps ... Basically we are using under 2000 Watts of power at any one time. I just got a second expansion battery and am currently charging it. We now have a 15kWh system. No solar, we gotta change it with a generator or a wall outlet. It does take almost 1800 watts to change via the AC charging cable, we have a dedicated 20 amp circuit in the house when there's power, or a dedicated 20 amp inverter generator power. I'm absolutely impressed with the ease of use. Batteries at night, Generator during the day. Hooray

    Jackery Explorer 5000 and STS

    I have the Jackery 5000 with the STS installed (no solar panels). So far I am very pleased with it. I have had it about two months and it has carried me through 2 power failures without issues. The first power failure lasted about 5 hours and the second was about 3 hours. In both cases I used less than 50% of the power. The system kept my network running and my essential circuits going without issue.

    My only issue was the cost of the installation. It was higher than I was estimating, but that was driven by the number of circuits I have backed up (10).

    In both cases, the system ran flawlessly! My previous backup (which I am keeping as second level fallback) is a gasoline generator. To start it, I previously, had to go outside (usually in a storm rain/snow) and start it, manually throw the transfer switch, then run extension cords around the house. Now, everything I need (network, fridge, critical circuits) switched without any actions from me! Great!

    20KWH whole home system review after 1 month

    All in all the 20KWH whole home system is amazing! It works effortlessly, carrys the entire home load, except i kept high load circuits like my electric clothes dryer and whole home AC unit on the grid for obvious reasons. Excellent product Jackery.
    I have noted a few potential concerns and have discussed with the tech team. Seems like a future patch is a potential to resolve them, otherwise i would give this product the highest score!
    If Grid goes down for multiple days, and you do not have solar charging the 5000’s, or if you do, but need some additional juice, there is no way to charge via the 110 cord, unless you manually disconnect the cable from the smart switch. The Smart switch disables this ability on the base units themselves. If you do not have a smart switch plugged in, this 110 A/C charging does work.
    When charging the 20kwh batteries via the smart switch, you are charging at 4kw per unit. So its an 8k draw until batteries are full. This is great in some cases. For me, due to a 2nd rack of solar i have thats tied to the grid at 120V this 8kw draw far exceeds what that system generates. I would love the ability to either charge at 8kw or bump it back to lets say a medium charge rate and cut it in half. That would maximize my solar generation and help reduce my electric costs.

    Those are the only two things that “I” would love to see the app approve on.

    If your looking to buy, this system is very good/solid and no general performance issues so far.

    Solar recharge only when power is out

    While the systems still need time to be tested, it seems it should perform power as it states. My issues is it only allows the recharging of the batteries when the power comes back on when hooked up to the automatic transfer switch. It’s hard to find this information through the internet sales sites. I only discovered this after it was installed.

    At this point when the system is discharging it can ONLY be charged by a solar powered input.

    Now it can be charged by a generator if NOT hooked up to a smart transfer switch through the supplied power cord, if you want to move it around the house and directly plug in into your appliances.

    So if you want to use it as a whole house power and backup system BEWARE it can only be charged by solar input while discharging and hooked up to a smart transfer switch.

    You would think that they would allow the system to recharge from a generator and not only solar when being used as whole house backup.

    Anonymous
    Wonderful alternative to Generacs!! But a few gripes...

    I love my Jackery 5000 units. I have two now, and the power they provide during an outage makes it feel like we can live almost normally until the power comes back on. Also had the Jackery ATS and a manual interlock switch w/30-amp plug put in (since the ATS only covers 12 switches the interlock switch can power the remaining switches).

    But it’s not without certain limitations. For one, the app itself feels limited (especially compared to its closest competitors). Aside from this, three serious drawbacks with the Jackery 5000’s that shouldn’t be the case are 1) All other Jackery units now use the better, longer lasting lithium batteries, whereas Jackery 5000’s still use the older lithium that doesn’t last as long and wears out faster. It’s almost unbelievable to me that their premier, flagship unit is also the only line that still uses the worst lithium battery technology. 2) Zero protection against humidity or high temperature storage locations… Seriously, it’s fine that these aren’t intended to be left outside- but when you can’t even store them inside of a garage in a moderate climate that’s a design problem and a serious foresight missed by Jackery. This should be rated higher for protecting these expensive investments from the elements. 3) All features (such as quiet charging) are greyed out on the Jackery 5000’s when connected to the ATS. There’s no ability to control the units at all unless you manually unplug them. Feels like there really should be an option to “digitally” unplug them for advanced features in the app.

    They’re also a bit heavy and hard to move around (forget it with stairs).

    None of those issues gives me buyers remorse though. For what these things can do they’re amazing. Just don’t expect perfection— go into the purchase with flexibility in mind and you won’t regret it.
